The fastloop runs while `in_next < in_fastloop_end`. Inside the fastloop, `REFILL_BITS_IN_FASTLOOP()` reads a full word (8 bytes) from `in_next` without checking the end. So if `in_next` is near the end of the actual allocation, this reads past the end.

The zlib header read at line 49: `hdr = get_unaligned_be16(in_next)`. This reads 2 bytes at `in_next`. For this to be READ 2 past the end, `in_next` must be at `allocation_end - 2` or later.

But `in_next` is the start of the buffer passed to `exr_uncompress_buffer`. For the UNKNOWN data, `in_next = compressedUnknownBuf = packed_buffer + 88`. For this to be at `allocation_end - 2`, `packed_buffer + 88 = packed_buffer + packed_size - 2`, so `packed_size = 90`. And `unknownCompressedSize >= 6` (for the zlib check to pass). But `packed_size >= 88 + unknownCompressedSize` (from the iSize check). So `90 >= 88 + unknownCompressedSize`, so `unknownCompressedSize <= 2`. But `unknownCompressedSize >= 6`. Contradiction.

So the UNKNOWN data zlib header read can't crash.

For the AC data: `in_next = compressedAcBuf = packed_buffer + 88 + unknownCompressedSize`. For this to be at `allocation_end - 2`, `88 + unknownCompressedSize = packed_size - 2`. And `packed_size >= 88 + unknownCompressedSize + acCompressedSize + ...`. So `packed_size >= packed_size - 2 + acCompressedSize + ...`. So `acCompressedSize + ... <= 2`. But `acCompressedSize >= 6` (for the zlib check). Contradiction.

So the AC data zlib header read can't crash either.
